LESSON: MIXTURES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: INTEGRAT ED SCIENCE
Strand: Mixtures, Elements and Compounds
Topic 2.1: Mixtures
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Mixtures, part of Mixtures, Elements and Compounds in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven INTEGRAT ED SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How is the separation of mixtures important in day- to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. separate homogeneous mixtures using appropriate method,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Mixtures in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. outline applications of separating homogeneous mixtures in day-to-day life,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Mixtures in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the use of different methods of separating mixtures in day- to-day life. ● Learners are guided to categorise the identified mixtures as homogeneous or heterogeneous which include solid-solid, solid- liquid, liquid-liquid and gas-gas mixtures. ● Learners are guided to brainstorm on the meaning of the terms solvent, solute and solution. ● In groups, learners share tasks as they carry out activities to separate homogeneous mixtures such as: o Simple distillation: Learners are guided to manipulate and identify apparatus used during simple distillation. Learners are supported in setting up and carrying out the experiment. Learners to feel the residue in the boiling tube and distillate in the test tube. How is the separation of mixtures important in day- to-day life? 11 ● Applications of methods of separating mixtures in real life o Filtration: Learners are guided to manipulate the residue on the filter paper and filtrate in the beaker. o Decantation: Learners are guided to feel solid -liquid mixture such as sand and water. Learners with blindness are supported to carefully pour out the liquid into another clean beaker. Learners feel liquid and solid after separation. o Use of a magnet: Learners are guided to feel solid -solid mixture such as Sulphur and iron filings. Learners with blindness are guided to feel magnetic materials attracted by the magnet and the substance that was not attracted. o Sublimation: Learners are guided to feel solid -solid mixture such as sodium chloride and iodine. Learners with blindness are supported 12 to set up the experiment and are given verbal descriptions on colour of the mixture, vapour and sublimate. Learners are guided to feel the sublimate on the lower part of the watch glass and residue in the beaker. o Paper chromatography: Learners with low vision observe the process of separation in filter paper strips. Learners with blindness are given verbal descriptions on location of baseline, solvent front and components of ink with their properties that make them possible to be separated through paper chromatography. o Solvent extraction: Learners with blindness to be supported on aspects of the experiment that require use of sight. 13 o Crystallisation: Learners are supported to feel copper(I

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Mixtures together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: The learner learns data presentation as they work collaboratively to categorise the mixtures as

homogeneous or heterogeneous.

14

mixtures.

Values:
● Unity: The learner works harmoniously with peers while carrying out activities to separate homogeneous mixtures.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Peer education and mentorship: The leaner practices sharing of tasks as they carry out activities to separate homogeneous

mixtures.
